sentences.text: Eosphorosuchus is defined by an unusually short snout built for a powerful bite. Its skull is short, robust, and taller relative to its length compared to relatives like Dibothrosuchus and Terrestrisuchus. The antorbital fenestra, an opening in the skull, is greatly reduced and nearly closed, likely to reinforce the bone structure. This predator also features a large, circular orbit and sharp, recurved teeth.
The animal possesses three osteoderms, which are bony plates in the skin, that are wider, more circular, and have a midline keel compared to its relatives.

Evidence of past violence includes a toe bone showing a healed swelling from a bite on the foot, while a swelling on the third metatarsal indicates the animal recovered from an injury caused by a tooth fragment embedded in its left foot.

The fossil material was discovered at the Coelophysis Quarry in Ghost Ranch, New Mexico. The fossil block containing the specimen was collected in 1948 by a team from the American Museum of Natural History.
Taxonomically, Eosphorosuchus is classified as an early member of Crocodylomorpha.
Eosphorosuchus lived during the Late Triassic, specifically the Rhaetian age. It is known from the Chinle Formation of Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.
Researchers suggest that the coexistence of Eosphorosuchus and Hesperosuchus in a mass death assemblage suggests they partitioned terrestrial carnivorous niches.
